title: Sorted keys meet a rotating tree
hook: Keys 1 to 7 arrive in sorted order. How tall does the search tree get?

knows: insert order shapes a search tree (lopsided-tree)
doesNotKnow: that a tree can fix itself with a local rotation and stay in order

misconception: Ordered input always gives a chain; the only cure is shuffling the input first.
objective: The learner can explain that a rotation lifts the middle key while keeping the left-to-right order, so a tree that rotates whenever one side is two levels deeper takes keys 1 to 7 in order and stays 3 levels tall instead of becoming a chain of 7.

claims.text: Inserting keys 1 to 7 in order, counting height in levels (a single node is height 1): a plain search tree becomes a chain of height 7, and a tree that rotates whenever one side of a node is two levels deeper than the other (AVL) ends 3 levels tall with root 4, after 4 rotations.
claims.source: Builder's node script (algo2-sd, 2026-10-14), standard AVL insertion: heights after each key 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 3; root 4; 4 rotations; plain BST heights 1..7. Same insertion as Demo.tsx. Matches the brief and company/design/specs/rotation-untangles-the-chain.md. Counted in edges the heights would be 2 and 6. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own node AVL (levels): heights 1,2,2,3,3,3,3, root 4, 4 rotations; plain BST heights 1..7.

claims.text: The four rotations happen at node 1 (inserting 3), node 3 (inserting 5), node 2 (inserting 6) and node 5 (inserting 7), and each is a single left rotation. At key 3, 2 rises above 1 and 3 and becomes the root.
claims.source: Builder's node script: unbalanced node at each rotation 1, 3, 2, 5 with the new key in the right child's right subtree (single left rotation). After key 3 the tree is 2 with children 1 and 3. Shown on the stage as the note 'Rotated at X: Y moves up' and the dashed ghost. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own node log: rotations at 1 (key 3), 3 (key 5), 2 (key 6), 5 (key 7), all single left; after key 3 the root is 2 with children 1 and 3.

claims.text: A rotation keeps the left-to-right order of the keys, so every search stays valid.
claims.source: A left rotation at x with right child y turns x(A, y(B, C)) into y(x(A, B), C); the in-order sequence A x B y C is unchanged. CLRS 4e (clrs-4e) section 13.2, Rotations. On the stage each key keeps its own column. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): x(A,y(B,C)) -> y(x(A,B),C) keeps in-order A x B y C; own node in-order check after every insert. CLRS 4e sec. 13.2 'Rotations' placement correct to my knowledge (not opened).

claims.text: Rotating whenever one side gets two levels deeper keeps the height close to log₂ of the number of keys.
claims.source: Adelson-Velsky & Landis (1962), 'An algorithm for the organization of information', Doklady Akademii Nauk SSSR 146: an AVL tree with n keys has height below about 1.44 log2(n + 2). Bound written from the brief; builder has not opened the paper (check before verifying). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own derivation: min nodes for height h is N(h)=N(h-1)+N(h-2)+1, giving h < 1.4405 log2(n+2) - 0.3277 (checked h=1..29 in node); any binary tree has h >= log2(n+1). 'Close to log2' holds within a factor 1.44. Adelson-Velsky & Landis 1962 (Doklady 146) not opened; sentence does not depend on it.

claims.text: In a plain search tree smaller keys go left and bigger keys go right, with no rotations.
claims.source: Definition of a binary search tree insertion (CLRS 4e ch. 12). Stage rule line in plain mode. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Matches the stage rule line and plainInsert() (BST insertion definition). | REOPENED 2026-10-14 (v4, phone fit build 6, demo-builder): stage rule line for the plain tree reworded from 'Smaller keys go left, bigger go right. No rotations.' to 'Smaller keys left, bigger right. No rotations.' (phone fit). Claim text unchanged; needs a fresh check of the stage wording. | FC pass 34 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14, W-375): VERIFIED. Independent of the drafter. plainInsert(): k < n.k goes left, else right, and the plain tree never rotates (snapshots('plain') rots = 0). Rendered (Playwright, 390x844) with the reveal opened in Plain mode (Insert next key, Insert the rest, Plain): rule line 'Smaller keys left, bigger right. No rotations.', the 7-level chain, Height 7 levels, Rotations 0; the reveal opened there quotes the recorded rotating result (3 levels, 4 rotations) and 'the plain tree was a chain of 7', true. Standard BST insertion; the stage shows it.

claims.text: Stage note after each rotating insert: key 3 made 1's side too deep, 2 lifted up; key 5 at 3, 4 lifted up; key 6 at 2, 4 lifted up; key 7 at 5, 6 lifted up. After key 3, 2 sits above 1 and 3.

Hand trace of AVL insertion of 1..7 agrees with c2. Builder, 2026-10-14. | FC pass 24 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. recall.question: A search tree rotates at a node to fix a lopsided side. What is guaranteed to stay the same?
options: The left-to-right order of the keys
Which key is at the root
recall.why: A rotation moves keys up and down but never past each other, so the in-order sequence, and every search, still works.
